newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks end week firmer, seen moving on.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks end week firmer, seen moving on.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks ended the week firmer in active trade and brokers said they expected the market to continue moving ahead next week as an issue by a local merchant bank which had tied up players' attention was now out of the way.
Brokers said indications were that the issue by the National Merchant Bank (NMB) which closed on Thursday was four or five times oversubscribed.
"A lot of people were looking at the new issue, now that it's out of the way I think we will see a lot more activity in the market. It will definitely pick up next week," one broker said.

The market's key industrial index rose 27.67 points to close Friday at 10,236.49, pushed higher largely by publisher Zimpapers' 250-cent surge to 5,250 and steel window manufacturer Radar's 40-cent rise to 500.

Also among the winners, pork processor Colcom gained 20 cents to 460, horticulture company Ariston added 15 cents to 220 while clothing and furniture retailer Tedco at 260, transport group Clan at 210 and fencing supplier CIH at 120 all put on 10 cents.
Against the trend, clothing retailer Edgars lost five cents to 770 and paper mill KCI slipped three cents to 117.
Minings traded firmer with Wankie Colliery up 15 cents to 540 and nickel producer Bindura jumping 30 cents to 780.
The mining index rose 21.38 points to 1,000.55.
